sections.h2: Your options for a quick sale
sections.html:
Cash money can arrive inside a month. A listing drags longer, though it may fetch more. Both work in College Station; pick by looking at what the house needs, who lives in it and how soon you need to be done.

Brazos County is home to this city, and Texas A&M University sits beside it. The school drives much of the buying and renting.

  • Cash contract: an as-is purchase where you name the closing day.
  • Agent listing: the biggest pool of buyers, paid for with showings and repair negotiations.
  • Investor sale: works like cash, and fits houses with renters already inside.
  • Keeping it as a rental: allowed, but you must register it with the city (see below).

College Station leans toward students. The 2025 estimate shows 127,472 residents, up 5.8% from April 2020, while only 35.4% of homes are owner-occupied (2020-2024). Just 66.1% of people lived at the same address a year earlier, which tells you how often student housing turns over.

sections.h2: Does a College Station rental have to be registered?
sections.html:
Mostly yes. Any single-family house, townhome, duplex, tri-plex, four-plex, five-plex or six-plex that the owner does not live in must be registered with the city, rent charged or not. Condos and buildings of more than six units fall outside the rule.

Registration costs $90 per building, paid once, as of October 24, 2022, and never renewed. If you live elsewhere you need a local contact who is off the lease and lives within 30 miles of City Hall.

Penalties run $25 a day for days 31 to 45 after notice and $100 a day from day 76. Municipal court fines range from $180 to $500, depending on how many offenses you have and how quickly you pay.

Selling a house that has been rented? Check with City Hall for unpaid penalties, which must be cleared before registration is complete.

Vacation and game-day rentals count under the city definition. So does a house where a relative lives and you do not. Pull the registration record before listing, then ask code enforcement if a separate short-term rental permit covers your address.

Values are set as of January 1 by the Brazos appraisal district. Appraisal notices arrive in several batches between April 15 and June 1. You can protest until May 15, or until the 30th day after your notice if that is later. Rates get set between July and September, and bills from the tax assessor-collector land in October and November.

Pay by January 31. From February 1 an unpaid account is delinquent, with a six percent penalty and one percent interest starting to build. The appraisal district office is at 4051 Pendleton Drive in Bryan, open weekdays, and exemption forms can go in by email to the address on its contact page.

sections.h2: Who owes the tax after a sale
sections.html:
A tax lien takes hold of the house every January 1, and the January owner stays on the hook for that year's bill after a sale. A buyer closing after January 1 can claim a homestead exemption at once if you never had one. Get a tax certificate before signing so the title company can split the year properly.

If a bill goes delinquent, the owner may ask the collector in writing to waive penalty and interest. Payment must come within 21 days of learning about the delinquency, and the written request within 181 days of the delinquency date.

A will can be probated for up to four years after the owner dies. An estate that needs no administration may use a muniment of title instead. Lenders sell foreclosed houses on a first Tuesday following a notice of sale, and a default notice leaves 20 days to reinstate. A sale closed ahead of that Tuesday lets you keep control of the price.

The county clerk records the deed, which must be acknowledged before a notary or two witnesses. Recording fees change, so ask the clerk for the current schedule.

sections.h2: A cash sale, step by step
sections.html:
A cash deal moves quickly. You send the buyer the address and deed details. One walkthrough later, an offer arrives in writing, priced for the house's condition. Say yes and the title company starts a file, searches for liens and asks each lender for a payoff figure. Closing happens on the day you pick, either in the office or by mail, and the wire reaches you once mortgages and any back taxes have been settled.

The deal skips the steps that stretch a listing: open houses, financing contingencies, appraisals that come in short and repair requests from inspectors. The tradeoff is price, because the buyer prices in repairs and risk. Request every offer in writing, then set it beside what a listing would leave you after commission, fixes and the months of carrying costs.

Demand tracks the Texas A&M calendar. Houses close to campus attract investors and parents buying for a student, and houses farther out attract families and university staff. Tenants in place? Hand the buyer the lease, the rent ledger and the registration record early, and state when the lease ends.

A house left empty between school years prompts condition questions. Fresh photos, a cleanout and a list of work already done help, and the utilities should be on for the buyer's walkthrough.

The median owned home is valued at $346,700, while renters pay a median of $1,194 a month. Mortgaged owners carry a median housing cost of $2,270. Those three numbers frame what a College Station buyer is weighing: buy and live in it, buy and rent it, or walk away.

If your house could rent well, an investor may pay for that income. If it suits a family, a listing may do better. Gather a few written offers and rank them by the net amount that would land in your account.

Start with the deed and the latest Brazos tax statement. Add the rental registration record if tenants have lived there, a mortgage payoff figure and a short list of known repairs. Buyers and title agents request all of it, and having it ready trims days off the path from accepted offer to closing.

Buyers here care about parks, the university and a short drive. Workers average 17.4 minutes getting to work, so put that near the top of your house description.

faqs.q: Do tenants have to register a College Station rental?
faqs.a: No. The duty falls on the owner. An owner who lives elsewhere must name a local contact who is not on the lease and lives within 30 miles of City Hall.

faqs.q: What does College Station charge to register a rental?
faqs.a: $90 per building, one time, as of October 24, 2022. Late registration adds daily penalties, so act before the first notice deadline runs out.

faqs.q: Where do I ask about a Brazos County exemption?
faqs.a: Contact the Brazos appraisal district by phone or email using its contact page. General exemption applications are due before May 1, and some special applications are due April 30.

faqs.q: When is the Brazos County protest deadline?
faqs.a: May 15, or the 30th day after notice if that is later. The notice itself prints your exact date.

faqs.q: Can I sell with a lien for back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company orders payoff figures and pays the balance from your sale funds.
